messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content: At a pressure of 10 kPa (≈0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water rises slightly above the normal 0 °C.  In fact, the equilibrium temperature for the ice–water transition at 10 kPa is roughly **+1.5 °C** (about 1.5 °C higher than the standard 0 °C at 101.3 kPa).
